facts.claim: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 says to bump the major version for incompatible changes, the minor for backward-compatible features, and the patch for backward-compatible fixes.
Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 says major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development: anything may change at any time.
Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 says a released version’s contents must not be modified; any change is released as a new version.
npm’s docs say package-lock.json describes the exact tree installed, so later installs can produce identical trees regardless of intermediate dependency updates, and it is meant to be committed.
npm’s docs say that with ignore-scripts set, npm does not run scripts specified in package.json files; it is off by default.
npm’s docs list preinstall, install and postinstall among the scripts npm install runs, and say the only valid use of install or preinstall is compiling for the target machine.
pnpm’s allowBuilds setting is a map of packages allowed (true) or not (false) to run their build scripts; packages not listed are disallowed by default.
This site’s own pnpm-workspace.yaml turns install scripts off for two of its dependencies, onnxruntime-node and protobufjs.
On 22 March 2016 a small package, left-pad, was unpublished from npm; installs of packages that needed it failed for about 2.5 hours, npm’s write-up says.

npm’s write-up says an attacker took over maintainership of event-stream and, on 9 September 2018, added a dependency, flatmap-stream, whose version 0.1.1 hid code aimed at a bitcoin wallet app; it was reported on 26 November 2018.
On 29 March 2024 Andres Freund reported a backdoor in xz releases 5.6.0 and 5.6.1, injected through their build scripts, that reached the ssh server through a library it loads.
